prompt_md: Flip a fair coin until heads-heads or tails-heads shows up on two flips in a row. Ann wins on heads-heads, Ben on tails-heads. What's Ann's chance?
prompt_short: Flip till HH or TH. Ann wins on HH. Her chance?
hint_md: Once a tail appears, can Ann still win?
explain_intuition_md: Both patterns are equally common in a long run of flips, so 50-50 feels right. But Ann can only win if the first two flips are both heads. As soon as any tail appears, the next head completes tails-heads before heads-heads can.
explain_math_md: Any tail means TH comes first, so $$P(\text{Ann}) = \left(\tfrac12\right)^2 = \tfrac14$$
